summary: Round 30 plan check, 01:15-01:35Z 29 Sep. All three night files were sent per the freeze (52 exp89r 00:05:28Z, 53 exp75 00:05:34Z, 54 exp89p 00:46:36Z), are PENDING at 01:13:57Z and are ledgered in the right families. The first read is exp89p at ~07:38-08:27Z. E10 is none, no knob was disclosed, rank 132 at 0.959. Two pre-score contradictions must be logged before exp89p can read (07:38Z = 10:38 MSK). (1) Card v5's tie order (1) literally picks exp87a because it has 'UP 12', while R26-A4 (d), in force via freeze (5), chains UPs by completion order. The two readings pick different FINALS when exp89p reads 0.959 with k = 0 (exp87a vs exp89p) or when several 0.959 files have UPs (exp89p vs exp89r). (2) Freeze (9) and card l.59 say 'SEC 0/- removes SEC from every morning file', but precedence (6) sends exp89q (K+SEC+DIS) on Rr '+' with DIS '?'. They collide at P 0.958 with exp89r 0.960. New facts: P '0u' cannot happen, because the LB shows the max over all submissions and exp89p at 0.958 cannot move our 0.959 row, so no UP call is needed at 0.958. SubmissionCount counts scored files only (53 with 3 pending), so the count-54 check is valid. nb_try's -v 1 is correct for exp89l, exp89s and exp89q (all v1). Ops gaps: the watchdog and the night read watcher are one-shot. The watchdog dies at the 05:10Z battery sleep, and the read watcher fires only on exp89p, leaving the exp89r A-M2 decision header unwatched. The E10 loop, the free LB-snapshot source, stops at 12:00Z. There is no stored morning submit block (tokens, -m texts, guards), and the count rule would wrongly MASK exp89r after exp75 completes unless the R26-A4 (b) exemption is applied.

findings.what: The V_pub tie order in finals card v5 contradicts the logged R26-A4 (d) rule, and the case where they disagree is the realistic one. Card v5 l.21 says: (1) 'the file after which WE passed teams (UP test; 0 passed = undecided)'. R26-A4 (d), which freeze item (5) keeps in force, says: 'An attributable UP chains by completion order; 0/MASKED/BLIND are unresolved, never lower.' Case 1: exp89p reads 0.959 (P '+', which also triggers A-M1) with k = 0. The literal card picks exp87a, because it has 'UP 12', but that UP was earned against the 0.958 state and says nothing about exp89p. R26-A4 (d) leaves the pair unresolved, so (2) 'no CI' picks exp89p. Case 2: two or more files at 0.959 each have an UP, for example exp89p at ~08:00Z and exp89r at ~09:30Z. The card goes to (2) and picks exp89p. R26-A4 (d) makes the last UP win, so exp89r. The chosen file is a FINAL, and V_pub CI vs non-CI also switches the pair structure (P3 {V_pub, #37} vs P1 {V_pub, exp75}). No night file has read yet, so the resolution is still pre-score.

The 0.959 block now has 22 teams and we are 18th (experiments/e10_watch/20260929T0113Z.txt), so a small unrounded gain can pass nobody and k = 0 is common.
findings.action: Before exp89p can read (07:38Z = 10:38 MSK), log one pre-score CONTEXT line and add the same sentence to card v5 step 5 (sha8 changes; note it in the line): 'TIE ORDER (1) = R26-A4 (d): an UP ranks a file only against our files already on the LB when it completed. Among files tied at the top display, X is above Y iff X completed after Y and X's completion gave an attributable UP (k >= 1; count +1, or the R26-A4 (b) exemption). An UP earned at a lower display (exp87a 12, exp85a 21) does not rank a file within its own display. Pairs left unordered (k = 0 / MASKED / BLIND) go to (2)-(4).' Consequences to state in the line: exp89p 0.959 with k = 0 -> V_pub exp89p (via (2)); with k >= 1 -> exp89p; a later exp89r/exp89l at the same display with k >= 1 -> that file. If the session prefers the literal card reading (an earlier UP counts), log that instead, but log one of them now.

findings.what: Two logged texts contradict each other on SEC in A-M2. Freeze item (9) and card v5 l.59 say 'P 0 or - removes SEC from every morning file'. The 21:11Z precedence item (6) says 'Rr + with DIS ? -> exp89q', and exp89q = K + SEC + DIS 2.25. They collide in exactly one cell: P = 0.958 (code '0') and exp89r = 0.960 (Rr '+'). Then dd = (0.960 - 0.958) - (0.959 - 0.958) = 0.001, so DIS is '?'. Row (6) sends exp89q, a file whose SEC just read 0, which is what (9) forbids. Other cells are consistent. P 0.957 with r 0.960 gives dd 0.002, so DIS '+' and exp89s (no SEC) goes. P '?' leaves SEC unread, and (9) does not apply. The A-M2 decision falls at ~09:25-11:00Z, after both reads, so choosing then is post-hoc.

findings.action: Log a pre-score line before 07:38Z that picks one reading. (a) Specific over general: '(9)'s SEC removal governs new builds (exp89l); the A-M2 Rr row sends exp89q as the non-CI twin of the submitted stack even when P = 0 (item (6)).' Then edit card v5 l.59 to say SEC is removed from new morning builds (exp89l) and that the A-M2 Rr -> exp89q row is the pre-registered exception. Or (b) strict: 'P 0/- -> A-M2 is UNUSED unless DIS = + (exp89s).' Do not substitute exp89s on DIS '?': that would be a new row. This choice changes only the (P 0.958, r 0.960) cell, and it must exist before the reads.

findings.what: P '0u' cannot happen, so the P code comes from the display alone. The public LB shows the team's best public score over ALL submissions: SELECTED is still {#37 0.954, #38 0.953}, yet our row shows 0.959 (exp87a). An exp89p display of 0.958 is below our LB best of 0.959, so it cannot move our row, and k = 0 by construction. The reachable P codes are '+' (>= 0.959), '0' (0.958), '-' (<= 0.957) and '?'. The same holds for any later file whose display is below the current LB best (exp75, and exp89r/exp89l at <= 0.958): their UP test is moot and costs an API call for nothing. An UP test is informative only when a file ties the top display (0.959 now), and then only for the V_pub order (PC30-01). The LB SubmissionCount counts SCORED submissions only: 53 at 01:13Z with 3 pending. So the 'count must be 54' check for exp89p is valid.

findings.what: The watchers are one-shot and nothing re-arms them. (1) The power/poll watchdog (PIDs 10576/25988) ends its loop with 'break' on the first ON-BATTERY or POLL-STALE alarm. It will fire when the laptop goes on battery for the 05:10-06:00Z trip and then stay dead for the rest of 29 Sep, including the 12:03Z/18:37Z proposals and the 19:43Z reminder. (2) The night read watcher (PIDs 13516/16292) waits until ANY of 56656147|56656157|56657612 is COMPLETE|ERROR and then exits. It will fire once, on exp89p at ~07:38-08:27Z. Nothing then watches exp75 (~09:03-09:48Z) or exp89r (~09:25-10:50Z), whose terminal header is the A-M2 decision header (latest 11:00Z). (3) The E10 watch loop exits at 12:00Z (run_e10_watch_loop.sh), so after 12:00Z there are no free hourly LB snapshots. They were the API-free S0/S1 backup and the card's RANK/BLOCK_POS source.

findings.action: (a) 06:07Z post-wake: once BatteryStatus = 2 (AC), re-arm the watchdog with the same text as a run_in_background Bash. (b) When the read watcher fires on exp89p, arm at once a second one on '^(56656147|56656157),.*(COMPLETE|ERROR)'. When that fires, arm a third on the remaining ref. At each morning submit, arm one on that ref (R29-A7). All are local-only reads of poll.log. (c) After 12:00Z, take the LB for the 18:37Z card and any tie UP test with python tools/uptest.py save <tag> (1 call each, <= 3 calls expected). Do not restart the E10 loop just for this (API load).

If A-M1 is UNUSED, the A-M2 label reads 'probe 55'; the token, not the number, matters. Guards before each submit: G1 header < 15 min; G2 used_today = 3 before A-M1 and 3 or 4 before A-M2, target token absent; G3 dataset baseline (ft-weights, n2a); G5 kernel COMPLETE, id match, no NEVER_SUBMIT. Then nb_try exp89l $KL "$M55L", or nb_try exp89s,exp89q <KS|KQ> <msg> for A-M2, so that neither variant can go twice. Do NOT rebuild or re-push exp89l at 07:23Z; only confirm the 22:16Z PASS line. After each submit, run the ledger and confirm the family: exp89l safetail_ci; exp89s/exp89q safetail.

findings.what: The UP-test count rule will wrongly MASK the exp89r read if exp75 completes first. The 07:23Z waiter says 'UP tests by the count rule', and R25-A1 (2) says 'count moves by 2 -> MASKED'. exp75 (~09:03-09:48Z) usually completes before exp89r (~09:25-10:50Z), so between an S0 taken at exp89p's read (count 54) and exp89r's S1 the count moves by 2. R26-A4 (b), in force via freeze (5), exempts a completion whose display is strictly below our LB display, and exp75 (~0.954) always is. An exp89r UP matters only if exp89r ties the top display, where it can move V_pub under PC30-01.
findings.evidence: research/wf_ideas_v4/round26/report.json R26-A4 (b) 'A completion whose display is strictly below our LB display before the window cannot move our LB row, so it does not mask'; CONTEXT.md l.3732-3734 (R25-A1 (2) count rule); experiments/lb_poll/ledger.md rows 56656157 (exp75, 00:05:34Z) / 56656147 (exp89r, 00:05:28Z), both safetail_ci; card v5 step 9 windows.
findings.action: If exp89r ties the top display: S0 = the newest of {S1_P, e10_watch snapshot converted per R29-A6 (hourly at :41 until 12:00Z)} taken before exp89r's terminal header. The expected count = S0 count + our completions in the window. A count jump caused by exp75 (display < LB best) is exempt under R26-A4 (b): write 'count +2, exp75 exempt'. MASKED only if another completion in the window displayed >= our LB best. If exp89r does not tie the top display, make no uptest call.
